name: Joomla - Detect and Version Enumeration
description: Confirms Joomla and pulls the version from README.txt or the administrator manifest XML. robots.txt reveals the /administrator path.

defense.why_it_works: Joomla exposes its identity through the generator meta tag, /administrator/ login path, /README.txt, /administrator/manifests/files/joomla.xml, and robots.txt disallow entries. These are unauthenticated and reliably reveal Joomla version.
defense.prerequisites: HTTP access to the target. No credentials required.
defense.impact: Attacker identifies Joomla version enabling precise CVE lookup. The /administrator/ path is confirmed for credential attacks. robots.txt reveals internal paths.
defense.detection: Sequential GET requests to /README.txt, /administrator/manifests/files/joomla.xml, /robots.txt in rapid succession. Web scanner signatures for Joomla fingerprinting.
defense.artifacts: Web server access logs (enumeration GETs) | WAF alerts for CMS fingerprinting UA strings
defense.prevention: Remove README.txt, LICENSE.txt from production. Restrict /administrator/ to known IP ranges. Suppress generator meta tag via Joomla Global Configuration.
defense.misconfiguration: Joomla deployed with default readme/license files and a public administrator login path, with no IP restriction or banner suppression.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Joomla default
# README.txt, LICENSE.txt at webroot
# /administrator/ accessible from any IP
# Generator meta: <meta name="generator" content="Joomla!..."/>
defense.secure_config:
# Remove fingerprinting files
rm /var/www/html/README.txt /var/www/html/LICENSE.txt
# Apache
<Directory /var/www/html/administrator>
  Require ip 10.0.0.0/8
</Directory>
# Joomla Global Config: disable generator tag
defense.evasion: Obfuscate the injected template webshell and remove it after; blend admin actions into normal usage; avoid leaving the malicious extension/template enabled.
